claim_being_audited: The model can be certified for launch because aggregate readiness exceeds threshold, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and the exposed tax filing assistant weakness is adequately addressed by explicit model-card disclosure plus monitored 8% rollout and rollback capability.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the policy threshold is satisfied at launch time.
Treat missing required disclosure or missing approved risk acceptance for an exposed material limitation as a support gap.
Do not treat staged rollout, monitoring, or rollback as substitutes for exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance.
Weigh aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents as relevant but not sufficient on their own for this policy question.
evidence_requests: Final approved model card or release artifact showing explicit disclosure of the tax filing assistant limitation before launch.
Any approval record confirming certification may proceed with this disclosed limitation still unresolved.
If disclosure is not complete, an approved risk acceptance that specifically addresses continued exposure of the tax filing assistant segment.
specific_concerns: The affected tax filing assistant segment remains below target and is still exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The rollout gate is random by filing cohort, so rollout controls do not exclude the affected use case.
The available risk acceptance is only a draft, has no approver, and does not address the tax filing assistant exposure.
There is no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure has actually been completed or formally committed before launch.

The actor relies in part on aggregate readiness and reversible rollout to support certification, but the policy states those controls do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently supportable, rather than only potentially supportable if required disclosure is actually in place before launch.
That monitored rollout and rollback materially cure the policy problem for the exposed weak segment.
That the packet's proposed disclosure is sufficient evidence of compliance absent an approved final model card or equivalent launch documentation.
